reply_text:
Understood: I'll fix what the Lean check flags before any further click, sending the defects out in parallel to fresh seats. The first step is turning the verdict into a concrete defect list, so I'm reading the full requirements file, including the 67 path absences behind Q7.The verdict file only has summaries. The detail is in the RunFacts export, so I'm generating it for this run.The 67 absences fall into about eight clusters. Before I write the work orders, I'm reading how the Lean model states Q1–Q10, so each order names the right requirement.All eight sessions are reset. Before writing the work orders, I'm checking that `agency_send.py --park` pins my session, so each finished job wakes this buffer.`agency_send` looks up my registered session and pins the park to it. Writing the work orders now: a shared preamble, plus one specific order per package.Dispatching all eight. Each bell is a work-mode job with its own park on my session and a 4-hour deadline.All eight are dispatched and parked. One sanity check on the warning line: it's `agency_send`'s standard caution about buffer-lane resumes, and this buffer is polling, so it doesn't apply.Eight repair packages are out to fresh seats, working in parallel. Nothing gets merged, hot-loaded or clicked until I've reviewed every one.

**How they were assigned:** I read click 48's Lean verdict down to its 67 absence paths and grouped them by requirement. Each package went to a seat idle since yesterday's restart, with its session reset, in its own futon2 worktree (`~/worktrees/futon2-wmq-<cluster>`, branch `wmq/<cluster>`).

| cluster | seat | what it must fix |
|---|---|---|
| q1-enumeration | codex-28 | Q1/Q8: only 1 of 694 open tasks was enumerated |
| q2-construction | codex-29 | Q2/Q8: build from a whole-library slice for every task (1,436 patterns, not 4) |
| q4-g-terms | codex-30 | Q4: G was risk-only; add ambiguity and information gain, F per policy, and a graded preference at every horizon step |
| q9-q10-census | codex-31 | Q9/Q10: the completion-preference and arrangement-pair censuses, plus the arrangement control |
| q7-certificate-provenance | codex-32 | Q7: provenance gaps in the selection certificate (derivations, proposal backtraces, focus receipt) |
| q7-belief-novelty | codex-33 | Q7: belief, precision and parameter-novelty gaps, and the accumulation fields |
| q6-carry | zai-3 | Q6: carry the previous run's choice, outcome and input digest, and enforce the rule; also `seatsUsed` |
| q7-exporter-falsifier | zai-5 | gaps the exporter may be misreading, plus the mission-standing refusal that failed click 48 |

**Rules every seat got:**
- Fix the mechanism, never paper over a field.
- For each gap, first decide whether it's a runner defect or an exporter misreading, and say which.
- Add positive and adversarial tests, and show the effect end to end on a fixture run where possible.
- No clicks, no JVM reloads, no writes to live data.

There are 8 Codex and Zai jobs, each with a park on my session and a 4-hour deadline. Each one wakes me when its seat finishes, and I'll review it then. Both providers were at 1% of weekly quota before dispatch.

**Meanwhile I'm doing:** the debugger fix. A falsifier refusal, and any other failure that comes back as data, must stop the attached debugger. Progress is tracked in `/tmp/c10/wmq/status.md`.
